_doc: What the shipped apps poll to learn whether they are behind. PER PLATFORM, because macOS and Windows do not ship together: a Store review can hold one back for days while the other is already live, and telling a Mac to update to a version only Windows has would send it to a store page that offers nothing. An app compares its own version with its own platform's `latest` and does nothing at all unless it is BEHIND — equal or ahead means no prompt, which is what keeps a TestFlight or internal build from nagging about a version it already contains.

_fields.latest: The newest version LIVE on that platform's store. Do not raise it when a build is submitted — raise it when the build is downloadable, or every user is told to fetch something that is not there yet.
_fields.minimumSupported: Advisory floor, currently unused by the client. Reserved for a hard cut-off older than any deadline below.
_fields.mandatory: The update must be taken within 72 HOURS. The clock starts when THIS INSTALL first sees the flag and writes the timestamp locally — not when the release was published — so someone who was on holiday gets their own full 72 hours rather than arriving to a locked app. Until the deadline it is an ordinary, dismissible prompt that says it is required; after it, the app asks them to update to continue.
_fields.criticalSecurity: The same mechanism with a 24-HOUR window and different words: the reason is named as security, so nobody reads it as a feature release worth putting off. Implies mandatory — setting this alone is enough.
_fields.store: Deep link opened by the update button. Both go to the UPDATES surface rather than the product page, because someone who already owns the app needs the update list, not a Get button.
_fields.storeFallback: Used when the deep link cannot open (protocol not registered, sideload, unpackaged build). Both are the real listings. Region-NEUTRAL on purpose: a /in/ or /gb/ path pins every reader to one storefront, and Apple already redirects a bare app link to the viewer's own.
